Photograph: Dan Kitwood/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A French warship and navy rib alongside an inflatable ‘small boat’ carrying migrants across the Channel after leaving northern France. Photograph: Dan Kitwood/Getty Images Immigration and asylum French officers halted small boats at sea 10 times since spring Disclosure challenges Conservative and Reform claims that police are refusing to intervene Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor Fri 7 Aug 2026 13.46 EDT Last modified on Fri 7 Aug 2026 14.31 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The French authorities have halted small boats at sea in the Channel on 10 occasions since the spring, officials said on Friday. Despite claims from the Conservatives and Reform that the French were refusing to intervene in small boat crossings, maritime prefect officers were using “intervention tactics” to board or control vessels at sea and take asylum seekers back to France . The disclosure comes as political parties are once again attempting to seize the initiative over small boats over the summer. Chris Philp, the shadow home secretary, last week confronted French police on a beach near Boulogne and uploaded footage to X of an officer saying: “Our order is to let them go. We just have to say to them, ‘Don’t do that. It’s dangerous.’” Earlier this week, Reform MP Lee Anderson visited Calais and said the French police were “literally waving these people on to boats”. In an unusual intervention, the director of maritime and small boats at Border Security Command, Charlie Eastaugh, said: “The incidents we have seen in the Channel over the last few weeks are a stark reminder of the dangers posed by criminal gangs exploiting people for profit. It is easy to look at out-of-context images and think little is happening to stop these crossings – this is simply not true. Has the UK government’s strategy on small boat crossings been effective? Read more “I know personally how tirelessly French officers have been working to disrupt launches before they reach UK shores. Their efforts include facing violent people with weapons, dispersing huge crowds, arresting smugglers, seizing equipment and collating vital evidence to help our prosecutions.” Every confrontation with asylum seekers was assessed by commanders as well as individual police officers and gendarmes, who were expected to balance the safety of their officers with that of the public, including large groups of often agitated people and gang members, officials said. On Sunday, when Andy Burnham visited HM Coastguard in Dover, Border Force officers had been warned that it was a “red day”, when conditions were calm enough for several small boat crossings. Two small boats attempted to launch from France, but one was intercepted at sea, while the other was halted on land. Small boats crossing the Channel were down by 43% compared with January to mid-July 2025 – from 21,690 people who crossed last year to 12,469 over the same period this year. The drop has come despite hot and dry conditions, which are usually associated with an increase in crossings. UK officials believe that government initiatives to “stop the boats” by financing the French authorities with another £660m in April have disrupted the business model of people smugglers in northern France and reduced the number crossing to the UK. Gangs are adapting their tactics. Boat launches have spread further along the coast, with some leaving from Belgium and others from as far south as Dieppe, a journey of 70 miles (113km) to the UK, compared with the Calais to Dover route of 27 miles. Officials are concerned the trend towards “mega-dinghies” – larger motorised boats – is putting more people at risk. More than 170 migrants were rescued on Tuesday after the boat they were using to cross the Channel caught fire. The sustained drop in crossings was a welcome development for Burnham, allowing him to focus his early weeks in government on setting out his policy agenda. Shabana Mahmood, who Burnham has kept in post as home secretary, has been reluctant to celebrate the recent drop because she is conscious the trend could change if there is an increase in arrivals in the late summer and autumn months. https://balkaninsight.com/2026/09/21/rom.text: Far-right firebrand Calin Georgescu faces fresh legal troubles as police investigate organised criminal group that allegedly defrauded a businessman of a million euros. Calin Georgescu at the Municipal Court in Bucharest, December 2025. Photo: EPA/ROBERT GHEMENT. Romanian police on Monday detained far-right politician Calin Georgescu and anti-fraud investigators searched his home and other locations as part of an investigation in which he faces charges of defrauding a Romanian businessman of more than 1 million euros, according to judicial authorities. “We carried out five residential searches … in a case in which three people acted with the aim of obtaining undue financial benefits,” said Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organised Crime and Terrorism, DIICOT. Prosecutors allege that from September 2021, a group allegedly led by Georgescu convinced the businessman that he could obtain a loan of 6 million euros in exchange for providing a guarantee. The victim then allegedly transferred some 1 million euros. Subsequently, the suspects allegedly told him that the loan could be increased to 15 million euro, but an additional guarantee was required, after which the businessman allegedly transferred another 100,000 euros. The promised loan never materialised. Georgescu has not issued any statement on this issue but he has previously claimed he was being investigated by the authorities because of his political activities. His political ally, George Simion, who heads the far-right Alliance for the Unity of Romanians, AUR, condemned the move. “Any of us could be next. Stop the abuses! Romania is a dictatorship!” he wrote on Facebook. Hundreds of Georgescu’s supporters gathered outside DIICOT headquarters, where he and other people were to arrive for questioning. Authorities have installed protective barriers and deployed gendarmerie units in the area. This would be the third criminal case against Georgescu. He is already under investigation for endorsing fascist ideas in interviews, online posts and public appearances and also faces trial for complicity to undermine the constitutional order, spreading false information and founding an anti-Semitic organisation. He denies all the charges. After he unexpectedly won the first round of the Romanian presidential elections in November 2024, the Constitutional Court ordered a rerun of the vote, citing alleged manipulation of public opinion by a “foreign state”, likely referring to Russia. Georgescu was banned from participating in the re-run in May 2025, which was ultimately won by centrist Nicusor Dan. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Plane makes emergency landing on Florida road Florida Small plane crashes into pickup truck on busy Florida highway No one was injured after emergency landing in Fort Myers 50 minutes after takeoff with two people onboard Keely Aouga Sun 8 Nov 2026 14.29 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A small plane crashed into the rear of a pickup truck as it made an emergency landing on a busy Florida highway on Saturday but miraculously no one was injured in the dramatic incident. Video footage obtained from the sheriff’s office shows a Cessna 172 grazing over the truck as it approached the ground for a complete landing on a road in Fort Meyers at about 11.45am on Saturday. The aircraft made an emergency landing after the pilot reported an engine issue, according to a Federal Aviation Agency (FAA) statement . All nine people onboard business jet that crashed in Florida have died Read more The plane took off from Sebring, Florida, around 11am on Saturday before it made the emergency landing about 50 minutes later, according to flight tracking data . There were two people on board the aircraft and the pickup truck was traveling eastbound on Bayshore Road. There were no reported injuries on the scene, according the Lee county sheriff’s office. “Couldn’t have been a better outcome. Grateful doesn’t come close!” Carmine Marceno, Lee county’s sheriff, shared in a post to X . LCSO Patrol & Florida’s department of transportation safely relocated the aircraft while the FAA is working to assume the investigation, Marceno added. The FAA is the lead agency on the investigation into the incident. The emergency landing comes one week after a business jet carrying nine people nose-dived into a south Florida neighborhood and erupted into a giant fireball. https://www.somersetcountygazette.co.uk/.text: Bristol Airport Ryanair Transport Somerset Ryanair launches new flight route from Bristol Airport Bristol Airport Ryanair Transport Somerset By Harry Mockridge Reporter Share 0 Comments Ryanair has launched a new winter flight route from Bristol Airport, starting this month. (Image: Martini) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. DISCOUNT flight provider Ryanair has launched a new flight route from Bristol Airport this month. The airline is now letting passengers fly to Warsaw Modlin, Poland, every Monday and Saturday. The new European city destination has been added to Ryanair's winter schedule, giving travellers from the South West another direct route to Poland's capital region. More: New holiday destinations launched from Bristol Airport for 2026 More: easyJet launches new holiday destinations from Bristol Airport Ryanair announced the service as part of an expansion of its operations at Warsaw Modlin Airport, where the airline is introducing several new routes for winter 2026. Warsaw is one of Poland's largest and most historic cities, known for its restored Old Town, royal palaces, museums and vibrant food and nightlife scene. It is described as an "exciting and memorable" city break. The new route is expected to appeal to both holidaymakers and business travellers, while also improving links between the South West and Poland. Speaking about the newly launched flight destination, a spokesperson for Bristol Airport said: "Flights to Warsaw Modlin with Ryanair are now flying from Bristol Airport "From its iconic skyscrapers to historic old town, Warsaw is a truly unique city full of character and culture. "Jet off every Monday and Saturday from BRS - book now." Flights can be booked through the Ryanair website and app. Bristol Airport Ryanair Transport Somerset Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading...
